points.requirement: Identity or receptor expression describes a useful product attribute but does not by itself establish tested biological function.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A cell-product lot is checked against specified quality requirements before its disposition. Identity, live-cell measures and biological activity answer different questions about that lot.
evidence.explanation: Current exact fields carry the specified distinction at the stated model, regulatory or inference scope. The current root separates identity/viability from product-relevant activity. Current FDA 2026 scope and the historical 2011 activity discussion are not a claim of clinical effectiveness. Current registered local-root representation; not main/live or independent acceptance.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Potency is relevant biological activity under defined conditions. FDA's November 2026 guidance aims for every released lot to have the ability to achieve the intended therapeutic effect and expects the relationship between a measured attribute and the product's mechanism of action to be supported by characterisation, nonclinical or clinical studies; where the mechanism is not fully understood, a statistical relationship such as a correlation with outcomes may help. Identity, receptor expression and viability do not establish activity.
evidence.explanation: Current exact fields carry the specified distinction at the stated model, regulatory or inference scope. points.requirement: A product-relevant activity comparison needs defined product-plus-target and target-only conditions, background and response controls.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Controls, reference material and handling state. Potency protocols should set predefined sample and system suitability criteria, and a run should be invalidated if system suitability fails. Reference material lots should be qualified and monitored for stability. Release assays must use a sample taken after all manufacturing steps that may affect potency, with cryopreservation named as an example, so a test on fresh material does not stand for the final product.
evidence.explanation: Current exact fields carry the specified distinction at the stated model, regulatory or inference scope. The root names suitability controls; complete target-only/background/response control detail depends on the actual unmerged cytotoxicity owner. The diagram supplies symbolic comparisons, not measured activity. Full representation requires actual unmerged contributor fields, with any root context kept separate; not main or root integration.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Method card, what it measures: whether specified effector cells cause death of specified target cells under controlled laboratory conditions, at a stated effector-to-target ratio and time. Readouts: flow cytometry that separates labelled targets from effectors and uses death-associated staining, release assays, or imaging over time. A fall in a metabolic or growth signal can reflect slowed growth and not death, so it needs validation as evidence of killing. Controls: target-only survival wells, effector identification and viability, a positive-control response, irrelevant or antigen-negative targets and suitable antigen or presentation perturbations, plus maximum release where relevant. Failure modes: high spontaneous death, mistaken target identity, aggregates, dye transfer, artificial loading, mismatched ratios or a readout that mainly measures growth.
evidence.explanation: Current exact fields carry the specified distinction at the stated model, regulatory or inference scope. The root names suitability controls; complete target-only/background/response control detail depends on the actual unmerged cytotoxicity owner. The diagram supplies symbolic comparisons, not measured activity. Full representation requires actual unmerged contributor fields, with any root context kept separate; not main or root integration.

points.requirement: A surrogate measurement needs evidence linking it to the relevant biological activity; quantity or expression alone does not supply that link.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Direct and surrogate measures. A direct biological assay measures activity such as target-cell killing; a surrogate measures a related attribute and needs a supported link to function. FDA's January 2011 potency guidance (now superseded) used the term assay matrix for complementary tests. The 2026 guidance recommends developing multiple assays that measure potency-related CQAs early, with redundant assays discontinued later. Many unrelated measurements do not add up to potency.
evidence.explanation: Current exact fields carry the specified distinction at the stated model, regulatory or inference scope. The historical 2011 guidance supports a surrogate linked to relevant activity and complementary assays. The current root explicitly marks that guidance superseded and distinguishes the 2026 approach. Current registered local-root representation; not main/live or independent acceptance.

points.requirement: Potency interpretation and release criteria are product-specific, under stated conditions and references, with no universal passing cutoff implied.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Reading a killing result. A figure such as 60 per cent killing is not comparable between laboratories unless target identity, effector-to-target ratio and observation time are stated, and relative potency needs a named reference and model. FDA's CAR T guidance describes orthogonal methods such as a cell-killing assay, transduction efficiency and cytokine measurement. No universal passing cutoff applies across products.
evidence.explanation: Current exact fields carry the specified distinction at the stated model, regulatory or inference scope. FDA 2026 distinguishes licensed from investigational contexts and phase-appropriate controls/criteria. The fixed 60-percent example in the root is an interpretation warning, not a cutoff. Current registered local-root representation; not main/live or independent acceptance.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Validation is about the assay, not the drug. The 2026 guidance asks that release assays measure potency with sufficient specificity, accuracy or precision over their reportable range, that performance be established under actual conditions of use, and that phase-appropriate acceptance criteria be set with failing lots rejected. Qualification and validation do not show that a drug improves a clinical endpoint.
evidence.explanation: Current exact fields carry the specified distinction at the stated model, regulatory or inference scope. points.requirement: The linked fictional two-hour example keeps 100 target events per condition and effectors outside the denominator: 40% minus 30% is 10 percentage points associated excess, not normalized lysis, individual-death causality or a patient-response prediction.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Background arithmetic, fictional: matched wells of 100 identifiable targets show 30% death without effectors and 40% with them at the same 2-hour endpoint. Raw death is 40%, but 30% occurs without effectors, so the excess is 40 minus 30 = 10 percentage points. That excess is associated with the tested condition and does not identify which deaths the effectors caused, and calling the result 40% immune killing is not justified. A control-normalised specific-lysis formula gives a different quantity from an excess-death calculation, so the method has to be named, and a high baseline death can make the experiment unsuitable.

points.requirement: Name the old and new process and properties affected by the change; a shared product or process name is not the comparison.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Comparable does not mean identical. Q5E says comparability shows that pre-change and post-change product are highly similar and that existing knowledge predicts that any differences have no adverse impact on safety or efficacy. First describe what changed and which properties it might alter, then use methods able to detect those effects. FDA's CAR T guidance says meeting current lot-release criteria is typically insufficient to establish comparability, and Q5E notes that stability studies can reveal subtle differences.
evidence.explanation: Current exact fields carry the specified distinction at the stated model, regulatory or inference scope. Q5E describes pre/post-change assessment of relevant quality attributes and effects on safety/efficacy. Its general biological-product principles are paired with CAR-specific guidance, not generalized clinical equivalence. Full representation requires actual unmerged contributor fields, with any root context kept separate; not main or root integration.

points.requirement: Where suitable, divide the same cellular starting material across old and new processes to reduce input variation without claiming all uncertainty is removed.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Where suitable, the same starting material can be split between the old and new process, for example one leukapheresis divided between pre-change and post-change manufacture (FDA CAR T guidance). This reduces one source of variation but does not erase all uncertainty or replace an adequate study design; healthy-donor material may be used in some studies, with patient-versus-donor differences considered.
evidence.explanation: Current exact fields carry the specified distinction at the stated model, regulatory or inference scope. FDA CAR 2024 PDF page22 recommends the same input where possible and explicitly discusses donor/patient variability. Splitting reduces one source of variation, not all uncertainty. Full representation requires actual unmerged contributor fields, with any root context kept separate; not main or root integration.
